> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57820085fa1cfb522fefc1e24e12f252d8d4630e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `db5554db0b387c443345867f27ff4077a05de307` — the merge of head `96844466d4db1163476073fbbe825875c0fe8d8e` into base `57820085fa1cfb522fefc1e24e12f252d8d4630e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin db5554db0b387c443345867f27ff4077a05de307 && git checkout db5554db0b387c443345867f27ff4077a05de307
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57820085fa1cfb522fefc1e24e12f252d8d4630e 96844466d4db1163476073fbbe825875c0fe8d8e && git checkout -B drift-repro 57820085fa1cfb522fefc1e24e12f252d8d4630e && git merge --no-ff 96844466d4db1163476073fbbe825875c0fe8d8e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57820085fa1cfb522fefc1e24e12f252d8d4630e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57820085fa1cfb522fefc1e24e12f252d8d4630e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `35d40a9e7bf52112cbdb9bd10cbca209bcb02b21`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-chart-bindings.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-chart-bindings.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.view-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-view-chart-binding.test.ts + packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts

Inputs: card #26847 (body, triage `6451024495`, claim `6451805787`, os-dev-report `6453550675`), PR #26906 (body, 9-file list, net diff against `main` at merge base `20457f6f`), and the 52 check-runs on the head: every required run `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 8/8, Build Core, Test UI, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness); the skipped ones are opt-in or `ui/`-only shards. No governed surface in the file list; the face is the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`validateChartBindings` row: `runtimeTypes` `['flow','report']` → `['flow','report','view','object']`** (`reference-integrity-suite.ts:454`). Right. `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor(type)` filters by this list alone, so a `view` and an `object` publish (`state: 'active'`) now run the member; `dashboard` and `page` stay out. The old comment's reason for excluding `view` (the snapshot carries no `reports`/`dashboards`) does not bite: on a view or object write `stack.reports` and `stack.pages` are absent, `recordsOf` yields `[]`, and the report and page surfaces find nothing. The one collection the list-view surface resolves against, `datasets`, is a `CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS` member every per-write snapshot carries (`runtime-gate.ts`), folded live from registry plus active `sys_metadata` rows and the batch's pending drafts (`protocol.ts` #15950/#16224, `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` `mergePendingDeclarations`). `datasets` are not package-closure-narrowed (only `objects` are, `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet`), so a dataset declared in any package of the deployment resolves.
2. **Accept-set at `PUT /api/v1/meta/view`**: a list view whose `chart.dataset` names no live dataset, or whose `chart.values[i]` / `chart.dimensions[i]` names no measure / dimension of it, is refused `422 INVALID_METADATA` (`chart-dataset-unknown`, `chart-measure-unknown`, `chart-dimension-unknown`, all `error` at the query position). Right: `ListChartConfigSchema` (`view.zod.ts:2093`) declares `dataset` as "Dataset name to bind", `dimensions` as "Dimension names (from the dataset)" and `values` as "Measure names (from the dataset)", so the refusal is the spec's own. The card asked for dataset and measure; dimension rides the same unchanged rule and is declared in the changeset and docs — right, not a scope creep.
3. **Accept-set at `PUT /api/v1/meta/object`**: an object's own `listViews.KEY.chart` is judged the same way on an object publish. Right, and it is what the card's "and `object`, for `objects[].listViews`" asked for.
4. **The two standalone view shapes** (`validate-chart-bindings.ts:630-640`): `viewKind === 'list'` with a record `config` → walked at `views[i].config`; `viewKind === 'list'` without one → walked at `views[i]` (flattened overlay). Right, and byte-for-byte the recogniser `validateListViewFieldRefs` uses (`:1346`, `:1356`). A `form` ViewItem is skipped; a ViewItem is walked at `config` only (pinned). Without these rungs the row change would have been a no-op for both door shapes, which is the card's fourth bullet.
5. **Early return now also checks `!stack.objects`** (`:372`). Right at the door (baseline and candidate both carry `objects`, so the guard is identical in both passes and the differential is unaffected). It is also live at `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint`: `authoringRuleUnionStack(normalized)` carries only the keys the manifest declares, so an objects-only manifest with no `datasets`, `reports`, `views` or `pages` whose `listViews` chart binds a dataset was previously skipped and is now reported `chart-dataset-unknown`. The verdict is right (the binding resolves to nothing either way) and is pinned ("refused, not skipped"); see ② for the one line of prose it affects.
6. **No false-positive channel opened.** On a view write the rule walks context `objects[].listViews` in both passes and their findings cancel in the candidate-minus-baseline differential; on an update the `stored` pass handles a sibling finding; `nameKeyFindingPath` keeps `views[0]…` positional (the written item is the sole member) and names `objects.NAME…` — both spellings are what the REST and lint pins assert. Drafts are untouched (D1 in `runtime-authoring-gate.ts`: `state !== 'active'` returns before any rule).
7. **Public surface**: no schema key added, removed or re-shaped; no export changes; `packages/rest` and `packages/metadata-protocol` source untouched — the door behaviour change arrives entirely through the `@objectstack/lint` registry row. Right.
8. **Re-judged pins**: the `view` and `object` member-surface rosters gain `validateChartBindings` with the measurement argument beside them. The #26719 door probes previously charted `status`/`task_count` against `duly_person_metrics`, which declares `name`/`person_count` (fixture at `validate-list-view-field-refs.test.ts:26-48`); `OWN_SELECTION` now selects each dataset's declared names so the foreign object stays the only defect — confirmed from the hunk. The #22491 REST file's `boot()` now `PUT`s the `lead_metrics` dataset through `type: 'dataset'` and throws if it is not `200`, so its control resolves — confirmed from the hunk (`call` gained a `type` parameter defaulting to `view`).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26847-list-view-chart-binding-publish-door.md` sits in the ROOT `.changeset/` directory (not `ui/.changeset`); `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- `'@objectstack/lint': minor`. Correct by the repo's rule (AGENTS.md §3): the kind decides the level — `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves; the pre-1.0 question does not arise (`@objectstack/lint` is `18.2.0` in the fixed group), and the rule fixes `minor` for a narrowed kind regardless. Only `@objectstack/lint` publishes a change; `packages/rest` carries tests alone.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are present line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and they agree. The triage note's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is superseded by the claim and the PR; the PR's pair is the well-formed one.
- BREAKING banner present; ADR-0087 marker present and single: `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason; `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:adr-0087-registration`) is `success`. The remedy paragraph (`**The remedy.**`) is present.
- `Clause-②:` line judged: **no (narrowing)** — right. The diff refuses at publish what published `200` before and widens nothing.
- **should-fix (prose, not level):** the changeset's "`os validate` / `os build` already refused it, and still do. Nothing is widened." overstates by one shape — per ①5 the early-return change makes `os validate` / `os build` newly report an objects-only stack with no datasets whose `listViews` chart binds a dataset. The level and kind already cover it; one clause in the "Before" bullet should say so.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: `[]`. Dev `out_of_scope_findings`: `[]`. Nothing to escalate.
- PR body "Not changed: `dashboard` and `page` writes still do not run this member; their surfaces are owned by their sibling rules." Answered: right. On those writes the surfaces the rule walks are the subject, `validateWidgetBindings` (dashboard) and `validatePageVisualizationBindings` (page) are the door rules, and the rewritten row comment says so. Not this card's gap.
- Claim `Premise: unverified at origin/main 20457f6f` — the dev re-measured through the real `RestServer` route on `20457f6f` (6/6 bad PUTs `200`) before editing; the REST block's header records it. Answered.
- Claim serial constraint (#26711 / PR #26851 narrows the `view` envelope in `packages/spec`): this diff touches no `packages/spec` file; no overlap in the file list. Answered.
- Card "measure the shipped view corpus at the door's snapshot shape before crossing": the row comment and the two roster pins carry the population (four example apps and platform-objects; two chart list views, 0 findings; lit probe refused at each door). The corpus measurement is the dev's account and cannot be re-run read-only; what the record can verify is that the two chart list views named (showcase `task` chart, `project` budget_chart) are the only `type: 'chart'` list views outside tests, which the PR states and the row comment pins. Accepted on the shipped pins plus the check-runs.
- Card "Pin a lit probe for each verdict at the door": done — 3 shapes × dataset/measure at `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (lint) and at the real route (rest), plus the object door, each with a clean control.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main` and the cited code:

- **Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. The spec declares `dataset`, `dimensions` and `values` of a list chart as names *from the dataset* (`view.zod.ts:2106-2116`) and the renderer (`ObjectView.tsx`, per the rule's own docblock) hands `values` to the dataset query as measures, so a binding that resolves to nothing never rendered. The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at the door, exactly as `os validate` already did. No implementation gap is being papered over: there is no declared capability to bind a list chart to an undeclared dataset or measure.
- **Live universe.** A tenant's dataset authored through `PUT /meta/dataset` (env-wide or the write's own org), a code-package dataset, and a pending draft dataset in the same batch all resolve (#15950, #16224, #10377). A draft dataset outside the batch does not — that is #7529's standing ruling (refuse at publish so author order is free), already in force for `report` (#19542) and for `validateListViewFieldRefs` at this same door (#26719). This PR opens no channel those two did not.
- **Differential safety.** Tried: a view write where a sibling context object carries a dangling `listViews` chart — cancels (same finding in baseline and candidate). An object update whose stored self had a dangling chart — `stored` pass marks sibling findings as pre-existing; findings on the written item are judged fresh, which is the intended re-judgement of a republish. A view write in a package scope whose dataset lives in another package — `datasets` are never closure-narrowed, resolves. A ViewItem carrying both `config` and a stray top-level `chart` — walked once at `config` (pinned). A `form` ViewItem — skipped. A list view with `chart` but `type: 'grid'` — same behaviour as `os validate` had on `views[].list`; not new.
- **Verdict path spelling.** `views[0].config.chart.dataset` / `views[0].chart.dataset` / `views[0].listViews.KEY.chart.dataset` for a view write, `objects.NAME.listViews.KEY.chart…` for an object write — located, and what the card's "located at `chart.dataset` or `chart.values[i]`" asked for.
- **Stored rows that no longer pass.** A view stored before this head with a dangling binding is served as stored and is refused only on its next publish, with the path and a hint listing declared datasets / nearest name. That is the narrowing the card ordered, with the remedy in the changeset and in `analytics.mdx`.
- **Findings:** no must-fix. One should-fix (changeset "Before" clause, ②). The code hunks hold against the code they cite and the scenario they are accepted against.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-27T21:51Z

Head `96844466d4db1163476073fbbe825875c0fe8d8e`. Card #26847 (seat-1 filing, triage `6451024495`), claim `6451805787`, dev report `6453550675`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on the `narrowing` face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, floor is every non-prose path). The review (`6453774408`) at `35d40a9e` was a PASS with no must-fix. It found:
  - The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real: `ListChartConfigSchema` declares `dataset`, `dimensions` and `values` as names from a dataset, and no declared capability is taken away.
  - Resolution reads the same live universe #19542 and #26719 already use at this door (registry, active `sys_metadata` rows and the batch's pending drafts), and the candidate-minus-baseline differential cancels sibling findings on a view write. Drafts stay ungated.
  - The two standalone shape recognisers mirror `validateListViewFieldRefs`, and the lint and REST pins cover every shape × verdict with controls.
  - The #22491 REST control now publishes its `lead_metrics` dataset, and the #26719 probes select declared names, so the foreign object stays their only defect.
  - The changeset sits in the root `.changeset/`. `minor` on `@objectstack/lint` is what the `narrowed` kind takes, and the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are present.
- **Since then:** `96844466` closes the one should-fix, changeset prose only. "`os validate` / `os build` already refused it, and still do" overstated by one shape. The changeset now names the two cases the CLI newly reports: an object's `listViews` chart in a stack that declares no datasets, reports, views or pages, and a `views[]` entry in the flattened overlay or ViewItem `config` shape. Level and kind are unchanged. The PR body never carried that sentence, so it needs no edit.
- **Shape:** `Fixes #26847`, 9 files, +331/−23. One root changeset, `@objectstack/lint` minor. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. `check-governed-merges --pr 26906`: NOT governed, 354 changed lines.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head are 40 success, 7 skipped and 0 red. `mergeable_state` is clean.
